chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abdul Hamid al-Wasiti, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May Allah keep you well. We have left our markets waiting for this matter, to the extent that one of us is about to beg with his hand.' He said, 'O Abdul Hamid, do you think that the one who confines himself to Allah, Allah will not find a way out for him? Yes, by Allah, Allah will surely find a way out for him. May Allah have mercy on a servant who revives our matter.'

I said, 'May Allah keep you well. These Murji'ah are saying that it is not for us to remain as we are until what you say comes to pass; then we and you would be equal.' He said, 'O Abdul Hamid, they have spoken the truth. The one who repents, Allah accepts his repentance, and the one who conceals hypocrisy, Allah will humble him (rub his nose). And the one who makes apparent our matter, Allah will shed his blood; Allah will slaughter them upon Islam just as the butcher slaughters his sheep.'

He said, I asked, 'So on that day we and the people will be equal?' He said, 'No. On that day you will be the pinnacle of the earth and its rulers. There is no leeway in our religion except for that.' I said, 'And if I die before I meet the Qaim (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'Indeed, the one among you who says,

key_terms.أَحْيَا أَمْرَنَا: Revived our matter, referring to keeping the cause of the Imams alive
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim, referring to the Twelfth Imam, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan
key_terms.الْمُرْئَةَ: The Murji'ah, a theological sect known for delaying judgment on faith and deeds
key_terms.سَنَامُ الْأَرْضِ: The pinnacle or highest point of the earth, indicating supreme status
key_terms.يَذْبَحُهُمُ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ: Allah will slaughter them upon Islam, indicating death while upholding the Imam's cause

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who wait for the Imam of the Age (Al-Qaim) and leave their worldly affairs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual merit of 'intizar' (waiting) for the Twelfth Imam, where scholars note that abandoning trade signifies prioritizing divine readiness over worldly gain. It contrasts the passive Murji'ah with active followers, promising that those who revive the Imam's cause will become 'sanam al-ard' (the peak/rulers of the earth), while even the deceased who pledged support are rewarded as if they fought alongside him, a concept central to Shia eschatology.
